conviction_note: The only in-window finding is a small positive: no issuer supply can land (+0.5). The number sits below it, at -0.8, because the reaction function outweighs it. The cause is a thematic AI-disintermediation sell-off with no company document behind it. This name's own closest analogue (2026-02-03, -15.24% in the Feb-2026 AI-disruption cluster) fell another -4.67% the next session. Own-history median is -1.21, and the Meta Connect keynote that could carry the theme further falls just after the window, which gives no buyer a reason to step in before it. The upside-paid skew (+1.08 lean component) is the only thing pulling the other way.

cause.label: sector_or_macro
cause.what_happened: In the 2026-09-22 afternoon session, lead-generation and marketplace names (EverQuote, LendingTree, QuinStreet, CarGurus, Cars.com, Yelp, LegalZoom) sold off together. The trigger was rapid adoption of Meta's autonomous AI agent Muse, No. 1 free app in US stores, with over 900k downloads in six days per Bloomberg 2026-09-21, which fed fears that agents bypass paid lead and ad funnels. EverQuote filed no 8-K and published no company news that day.

evidence.claim: StockStory dated 2026-09-22: stocks fell in the afternoon session on Meta Muse adoption fears. It names EverQuote among the lead-generation and marketplace names that traded lower together.
Muse topped the US charts with over 900,000 downloads in six days after its 2026-09-08 launch.
EDGAR shows no EverQuote filing between 2026-09-18 and 2026-09-22. The last was a Form 4 on 2026-09-17 and the last 8-K was on 2026-08-03 (Q2 results).

Search snippets place QuinStreet down about 9.8% on the same Tuesday session. This is a peer move, not a price of EVER; the snippet's timing relative to the screen instant is unknown, so only its sign is used.

pipeline.next_dated_event: Meta Connect 2026 keynote (Zuckerberg), 2026-09-23 at 16:00 PT / 19:00 ET, three hours AFTER the window's closing print. Nothing company-specific is dated inside the window.
pipeline.what_would_change_my_mind: Three things would move this: an issuer 8-K or a defending sell-side note before the 09-23 open, which would give the repricing leg a mechanism; or a second leg of the AI-agent theme during the 09-23 session, such as a Muse insurance or lead-gen integration announcement or pre-Connect disclosures, which would push it further negative.

findings.finding: No issuer supply can price tonight. EverQuote has never used at-the-market language in any filing and has no going-concern language. It had $192.3M of cash and no debt at 2026-06-30, and no 8-K clock is running on a drop-day event. So the offering, ATM or financing second shoe that drives much of the base-rate continuation cannot land between the 09-22 close and the 09-23 close.
findings.mechanism_in_window: It lands in the window by absence. The overnight window is when a fallen issuer's offering or ATM draw would price, and the 09-23 session is when it would show up. The baseline's efts probes find zero hits ever for '"at-the-market"' and '"substantial doubt about its ability to continue"', and EDGAR shows no 8-K since 2026-08-03. So the supply channel that separates continuing fallers from the rest is shut for this name through 2026-09-23.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None of this name's five comparable falls (2023-11-02, 2025-04-04, 2025-05-06, 2026-02-03, 2026-05-06) was followed by an equity issue; the filing record carries no S-1, S-3 takedown or 424B in the baseline's filing list. The next-close median across those falls is still -1.21%, so the absence of supply has not by itself produced bounces here.
findings.why_not_priced: The drop is thematic and the tape has priced a sector re-rating. The cross-sectional base rate the price is implicitly marked against (-1.00% median next session) includes fallers with open ATMs and going-concern clocks, and this name has neither. If the price already held this, EVER's comparable-fall history would show more up days than the pool; it shows 40% up, which is about the pool's rate. So the edge is small, and it is relative to the other fallers, not absolute.
findings.independence: The 10-Q for Q2 2026 is a different document from the text probes. It shows $192,318k cash and no debt on the balance sheet: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1640428/000119312526332775/ever-20260630.htm

outside_window.finding: Meta Connect 2026 keynote on 2026-09-23 at 16:00 PT / 19:00 ET, with Muse AI expected to feature. It is the next dated catalyst for the same AI-agent disintermediation theme that caused the fall, and it lands three hours after the window's closing print. Any agentic-commerce or insurance or lead-gen integration news would hit the 09-24 session. Negative skew for a lead-gen name.

The fall looks like an overshoot on fundamentals. Q2 2026 set a revenue record ($195.1M, +25%), Q3 revenue was guided to $198-208M, and the company holds $192M of cash, no debt, and has repurchased $50M of stock. But there is no mechanism dated inside the window, so this is not a finding. Next dated test: Q3 results, estimated 2026-11-02 by Zacks's cadence algorithm, which is NOT a company announcement.

Insider 10b5-1-style selling continues. Form 144 was filed 2026-09-15 and Form 4 on 2026-09-17 (CEO Jayme Mendal sold 20,981 shares per MarketBeat); Nasdaq shows 19 sells and 0 open-market buys over three months. These are small, recurring supply that is not dated to the window.

baseline_tension: What I found agrees with the reaction function rather than cutting against it. Volume at 3.7x says something was learned, but what was learned is a sector narrative, not a company fact. The closest own-history analogue (the Feb-2026 AI-disruption drop) continued -4.67%, and the only contrary signal is a thin-chain upside skew. So the +0.5 supply finding is overridden to -0.8, a 1.3-point haircut from the findings sum.
